chunk_findings.detail: `launch_env` always maps the child key variable to that same name (`{ep.api_key_env: ep.api_key_env}`) whenever `api_key_env` is set, and `Prepared` / the opencode launch pass that map as `LaunchSpec.env` together with `secret_env`. `secret_env` still resolves “variable first, then key file” into the same child variable. `LaunchSpec.env` is defined as a live source-name lookup that refuses the launch when that name is missing. Given an endpoint whose key is only in the key file (`api_key_env` set, process environment unset, file readable), prepare succeeds with a real value in `secret_env`, then launch refuses because `env` demands the unset variable. Previously `env` was `{}` and only the resolved secret was passed, so the file-backed key ran. The same overlap also keeps a prepare-time snapshot in `secret_env` after the source variable is revoked, so the “refuse rather than run stale” behavior is not actually enforced by this change.

chunk_findings.detail: `launch_env` returns `{}` whenever `api_key_file` is set, even if `api_key_env` is also set. `secret_env` still resolves “variable first, then key file” and snapshots that value at prepare time. Given `api_key_env="GEMINI_API_KEY"` (set) and `api_key_file` pointing at a key file, prepare injects the env value via `secret_env` and passes an empty `LaunchSpec.env`. Unset `GEMINI_API_KEY` before launch and the launcher does not refuse, so the child runs on the stale snapshot.
